simple.meaning: רֹאשׁ (rôʼsh) is a Hebrew animal word meaning “a poisonous plant , probably the poppy (from its conspicuous head); generally poison (even of serpents).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Deuteronomy 29:17. The surrounding context includes family line.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to רֹאשׁ (H7219) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: רֹאשׁ (rôʼsh) / H7219 is traced through Deuteronomy 29:17, Deuteronomy 32:32, Deuteronomy 32:33, Job 20:16 with generated occurrence evidence.
